COT report questions

What is the COT report?

The Commitments of Traders report is published every week by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). It shows how different groups of traders are positioned in US futures markets. This page uses the non-commercial group, the large speculators such as hedge funds, because they tend to ride trends.

When is the COT report released?

Every Friday at 3:30pm US Eastern time, covering positions as of the Tuesday before. After a US public holiday it can come out a day or two late. This page updates automatically soon after each release.

What is the COT index?

It places this week's net position in its range over the last three years: 0 is the most short speculators have been in that time, 100 the most long. Readings of 10 or below, or 90 or above, are flagged as extremes, where the trade is crowded and more likely to unwind.

How should I trade with it?

Not on its own. COT is slow, weekly data that tells you which way the big money leans. Use it to pick a side, then wait for price to reach a strong daily or weekly supply or demand level before you act. QDB pairs it with retail sentiment for that reason: when the crowd and the speculators disagree at a key level, that is where the best setups appear.

Can I use this data in my own sheet?

Yes. The numbers are free as markets CSV, pairs CSV and JSON. In Google Sheets, use =IMPORTDATA("https://quasidb.github.io/data/cot-markets.csv").

COT is the slow picture. Retail sentiment is the fast one.
